component.name: Tretlager
component.summary: Set up Zwift on Linux and connect your sensors
Zwift unter Linux einrichten und mit Sensoren verbinden

description.p: Tretlager sets up the official Zwift Windows client with its own Wine, starts it with one click and connects smart trainers and heart rate straps through a Bluetooth bridge that presents them to Zwift as Wahoo Direct Connect devices.
Tretlager is not affiliated with Zwift Inc. Zwift does not support Linux; use at your own risk.
Zwift may not be happy that a software bridge sends data that could be manipulated; restrictions up to a suspended account, including the XP and drops earned, cannot be ruled out.
Not for races: there is no guarantee that the sensor bridge passes power, cadence and heart rate to Zwift correctly. Do not use Tretlager for races or competitions with results.

Setting up the system works on Ubuntu: the WineHQ key is accepted and Ubuntu gets the matching Wine builds. Icons and colors follow the desktop outside Plasma, and the Debian package lists all the modules it needs.
The overview says when Zwift is being updated, and the warning about the Garmin HRM-Pro on the Intel AX201 is gone: with 0.11.2 the strap connects there too.
Sensors show that they were found while they are being read, and slow heart rate straps get more time to reconnect.

Heart rate straps come back by themselves after a dropout or a break out of range, instead of hanging until the Bluetooth adapter is replugged. A screen-on option for the ride and a warning when headphones share the Bluetooth adapter.

ul.li: Error reports: detailed logging and one ZIP file with system information and logs to send to the developer; sign-in data is removed.
Zwift opens on the monitor it was last used on and is maximised only once it has loaded; its picture no longer sticks out over the screen edge.
Wine's output of Zwift and the sensor bridge's messages are kept in log files.
Warnings on first start: not an official Zwift app, at your own risk, not for races.
Works outside Plasma: Breeze style, follows light/dark mode and the desktop font on GNOME.
Sign-in window fixed in the Flatpak.
Graphics setup notices when an NVIDIA card is switched on or off.
The sensor bridge connects the trainer first and gives up on absent sensors sooner.
English is the source language; German translation included.

description.p: More reliable sensor bridge and simpler updates.

ul.li: An absent sensor no longer blocks Bluetooth for the others; short dropouts keep the device paired in Zwift.
Before every start Tretlager checks the setup and adapts the Zwift environment to a new Wine.
The last proven Wine version is kept and can be used again after an update.
Download progress from the Zwift manifest for the first installation and for updates.
Overview with readiness, prominent start button and sensor values as key figures.
Notice: not for races, values from the bridge are not guaranteed.
